messages:
maria: quick ping — after I merged the values tweak into staging the app pods come up but complain about missing SERVICE_URL / FEATURE_FLAG keys. I changed chart to use envFrom for the config secret instead of listing env vars individually. anyone know if helm/ k8s can cause precedence problems here? @jess @tim :eyes:

jess: can you paste the values snippet + template? envFrom should populate all keys but if you also set explicit env entries they override the envFrom ones. also watch for empty-string vs missing keys.

maria: sure — values.yaml snippet:

```yaml
serviceConfigSecret: my-service-config
useEnvFrom: true
explicitEnv: {}
```

and template in deployment.yaml:

```yaml
envFrom:
  - secretRef:
      name: {{ .Values.serviceConfigSecret }}
{{- if .Values.explicitEnv }}
env:
{{ toYaml .Values.explicitEnv | indent 10 }}
{{- end }}
```

pods show logs like: "missing env: SERVICE_URL" even though secret has SERVICE_URL key.

tim: a couple quick checks: 1) confirm secret exists in the same ns (kubectl get secret -n staging my-service-config -o yaml) 2) check for keys with trailing newlines or CR chars — those can look weird 3) envFrom loads strings as-is; if explicit env mapping exists with empty value it will override an envFrom value.

maria: secret is there, keys look fine when I `kubectl get secret -o jsonpath='{.data.SERVICE_URL}' | base64 -d`. no empty explicit envs in values.

jess: hmm — one more gotcha: if you have both envFrom and env entries with the same name, the last one wins depending on how the runtime exposes them (container runtime merges). In your template the envFrom comes first then env, so env should win, but if explicit env has an empty string it would remove the value. Also check if a different chart-level default is injecting env elsewhere (subchart or sidecar).

devon: also — we recently introduced ExternalSecrets for team configs. If the secret is created by external-secrets, sometimes Helm create+deploy race: helm deploy finishes before external-secrets populates keys, resulting in envs present but empty at container start. We solved this elsewhere by either making ExternalSecret create the secret synchronously (provider setting) or by adding a simple init container that loops until the secret has the expected keys.

maria: ah — yes this secret is managed by ExternalSecrets. logs from external-secrets say "secret created" ~5s after pod started. so race is likely. Would an init container checking for key presence be the right path?

tim: yep that is low-friction. Example tiny init container (busybox):

```yaml
initContainers:
- name: wait-for-config
  image: busybox
  command: ["/bin/sh", "-c", "i=0; until kubectl get secret {{ .Values.serviceConfigSecret }} -o jsonpath='{.data.SERVICE_URL}' >/dev/null 2>&1 || [ $i -gt 30 ]; do sleep 1; i=$((i+1)); done; exit 0"]
```

(just ensure RBAC allows pod to read secrets or use projected volume check instead).

jess: alternative: change ExternalSecret provider config to populate the secret before helm rollout (we did that for prod). Or add `optional: true` on envFrom and then fallback to a configmap/values default. But optional means envFrom won't error — it just won't add keys.

devon: if you prefer templating-only fix, you can guard with `hasKey`/`lookup` in the chart to only add envFrom when secret exists. Example:

```gotemplate
{{- $s := lookup "v1" "Secret" .Release.Namespace .Values.serviceConfigSecret -}}
{{- if $s }}
envFrom:
  - secretRef:
      name: {{ .Values.serviceConfigSecret }}
{{- end }}
```

that prevents injecting envFrom when secret is missing (so pods still start with defaults) but it doesn't solve late-population race.

maria: nice, thanks. I think simplest is add initContainer that waits for key, and add the lookup guard as a belt-and-suspenders. I'll open a tiny PR.

infra-bot: deploy/staging/my-service started: pod/my-service-5f6b7c running. CI: 122 ✔️

maria: thanks all! will ping when PR is up. :tada:
